_: Per-quest dialogue in each villager's own voice. offer: lines before the choice. yes/no: reply to the choice. wait: nudge while pending. done: lines on turn-in.

offer: Five turnips. That's all I'm asking.
The display bin's been empty since the frost and people keep touching the empty bin, like it'll help.
maple_turnips.yes: Bless you. Pull them when the tops are fat, not before.
maple_turnips.no: Mm. The bin will wait. It's good at that.
maple_turnips.wait: Turnips, dear. Fat ones. The bin's still empty.
done: Oh, look at them. Look at them!
Right in the front, where Gideon has to see them when he walks past.
Here. For your trouble, and a little for your patience.

offer: Copper. Ten ore.
Not for anything fancy. Hinges. Half this town's doors hang crooked and it's mine to fix, apparently.
gideon_copper.yes: Good. Copper's in the mountain rock. Swing hard.
gideon_copper.no: Suit yourself. The doors can creak another month.
gideon_copper.wait: Ten copper. The hinges aren't getting any straighter.
done: That'll do.
...That'll do fine, actually. Clean ore. You've a decent arm.
Two bars off the top for you. Don't tell anyone I'm generous.

offer: I'm out of wild herb. Completely. I used the last of it on Bram's knee and he hasn't said thank you.
Six bundles would set me right. They grow where the grass goes long.
wren_herbs.yes: Thank you. Pick the ones with the darker leaves, they keep.
wren_herbs.no: That's alright. I'll send Wren jr. She'll come back with frogs.
wren_herbs.wait: Six wild herb, when you can. The jar's still empty.
done: Oh, these are lovely. Dark leaves, you listened.
Here, take some of the remedy, it's the first batch and you earned the first batch.

offer: Bass. Three of them.
I'll be honest, this isn't a job. It's a bet. Bram says you can't. I said you could. There's a pie on it.
finn_fish.yes: Ha! Knew it. They sit under the north bridge in the mornings.
finn_fish.no: Bram will be insufferable. Fine. Fine.
finn_fish.wait: Three bass. Bram's already practising his gloating face.
done: THREE. Look at that. Look at Bram's face. Where's Bram? Somebody get Bram.
Here's your cut of the pie money and a tin of bait. We'll do this again.

offer: Fence is down on the west side. Goat went through it like it was a suggestion.
Thirty wood and I can have it up before she does it again.
hazel_wood.yes: Good. You're alright, you know that?
hazel_wood.no: Fair enough. I'll tie it with string and pray.
hazel_wood.wait: Still thirty wood short. The goat says hello.
done: Here, hold this end. ...Done. Look at that. Straight as a sermon.
Wheat seed, for you. First of the season. Don't drown it.

offer: I keep starting the same painting. A field. It needs more flowers than I have in my head.
Eight wildflowers? Any colour. I'll mix the rest.
lumi_flowers.yes: Thank you. Pick them in the morning, they hold their colour.
lumi_flowers.no: That's alright. I'll paint the fog instead. Again.
lumi_flowers.wait: Eight flowers, when you find them. The canvas is waiting. Patiently. Unlike me.
done: Oh. Oh, these. Look at the purple on that one.
It's finished. You should have it. It's yours anyway, it's got your flowers in it.

offer: There's a mushroom in the old herbals. Luminous. 'Glow-cap'. Every book says it's extinct and every book is wrong about something.
If you find one, I'd like to see it before anyone eats it.
theo_glowcap.yes: Excellent. The forest, after dark. Bring a lantern, and then put the lantern out.
theo_glowcap.no: Understandable. Extinct things are poor company.
theo_glowcap.wait: No glow-cap yet? The forest, after dark. The books insist.
done: It's real. It's REAL. Look, it's still... it's faintly... do you see it?
I'm going to write a very smug letter to the capital. This is for you.

offer: The fountain's cracked on the north rim. It leaks into the plaza and people blame me, personally.
Forty stone and the mason will do the rest. The town will remember it. I'll make sure the town remembers it.
alder_stone.yes: Splendid. Mountain stone, if you can. It takes the frost better.
alder_stone.no: Of course. It's a lot of stone. The leak can wait. It's been waiting since before I was mayor.
alder_stone.wait: The fountain, when you have the stone. Forty. I've got a man ready.
done: Forty. Exactly forty. You're a precise person. I like precise people.
Payment from the town's purse, with my thanks, which are worth less but mean more.

offer: Two trout and a pumpkin. That's the stew. That's the whole secret.
Bring me those and I'll show you how it goes together. Nobody else gets to see that.
bram_stew.yes: Good. Trout from the river, pumpkin from... wherever pumpkins come from. A farm. You've got a farm.
bram_stew.no: Your loss. The stew is very good.
bram_stew.wait: Two trout, one pumpkin. The pot's already on.
done: Right. Watch. No, watch. ...And that's it. That's the stew.
Take two bowls. The recipe's in your head now, don't lose it.

offer: I need honey. Two jars. There's a cough going round the children and honey's kinder than anything in my cabinet.
I'd ask Hazel but she's got her hands full with a goat.
juniper_honey.yes: Thank you. Hives if you have one; Hazel builds them. There's a wild one up in the orchard hills.
juniper_honey.no: I understand. I'll manage with warm water and stern looks.
juniper_honey.wait: Honey, when you can. Two jars. The cough's still going round.
done: Perfect. Pip will stop coughing on the lectern now, thank goodness.
Here. Two of the good potions. Keep them for when it's you coughing.

offer: You're going to find rolled bills on those thugs. Don't spend them. They're marked.
Bring me five rolls. I know who's marking them, and I know who to show.
sal_cash.yes: Smart. Keep your head down and your pockets closed.
sal_cash.no: Fine. But if you find them, don't spend them. I mean it.
sal_cash.wait: Five rolls. Marked ones. You'll know them when you see them.
done: ...Yeah. That's his mark. That's him.
I owe you. Here. And now I owe you less.

offer: Spring display! I do one every year and every year it's better than Gideon's, which is nothing, because he doesn't do one.
Eight strawberries, the red ones, the really red ones.
maple_strawberries.yes: Oh good. The window's going to look like a postcard.
maple_strawberries.no: Mm. The window can be mostly ribbon then.
maple_strawberries.wait: Strawberries for the window, dear. Eight. Really red.
done: Would you LOOK at that window. Posy's already jealous, I can tell by her walk.
Here you are. Spring money.

offer: Summer stand needs corn. Ten ears. The stand is a plank and two barrels but people love it.
I'd grow it myself but then who'd stand behind the plank?
maple_corn.yes: You're a treasure. Big ears, please. People judge corn by the ear.
maple_corn.no: The plank will be lonely. Fine.
maple_corn.wait: Ten corn. The plank is ready. The barrels are ready.
done: Ten! And look at the size. Hazel's going to ask what you feed it.
Here. And melon seed, since you clearly know what you're doing.

offer: Harvest window. Three pumpkins. Big ones go in the middle, I put a little hat on the biggest.
Don't ask about the hat.
maple_pumpkins.yes: Wonderful. Big, round, no soft spots.
maple_pumpkins.no: The window will be... leaves, then. Leaves and a hat.
maple_pumpkins.wait: Three pumpkins, dear. The hat is waiting.
done: There he is. There's the one that gets the hat.
Here. Harvest money. You've made my autumn.

offer: Honey! I'm out, Posy's out, the whole street's out, and Juniper keeps buying it for coughs.
Four jars and I'll have a shelf again.
maple_honey.yes: Thank you. The bees like you, I can tell.
maple_honey.no: I'll put up a little sign. 'NO HONEY'. People will sigh at it.
maple_honey.wait: Four honey, when the hives give it up. The sign's still up.
done: Four! Down comes the sign. Up goes the honey.
Two pies for you. Posy made them with the honey I don't have. Don't think about it too hard.

offer: The back shelves came down. All of them. Forty years of shelf and they chose market morning.
Twenty wood, ten stone, and I can rebuild them properly this time.
maple_supply_run.yes: You dear. I'll clear the floor.
maple_supply_run.no: I'll stack things on the floor. It'll be a sort of... market.
maple_supply_run.wait: Wood and stone for the shelves, when you can. Twenty and ten.
done: Oh, they're up. They're UP. Straight, too. Gideon's never built a straight shelf in his life.
Here. And you've learned something about shelves, I can tell.

offer: Commission. Five iron bars. Somebody wants a gate with their name on it.
I'll make the gate. I won't do the name.
gideon_iron.wait: Five iron bars. The gate's still in my head.
done: ...Good bars. Even. You've been practising.
Steel, for you. One bar. Don't waste it on a hinge.

offer: Forge is cold. Fifteen coal.
I can't work cold. Nobody can. Even the hammer complains.
gideon_coal.no: Then it stays cold. Good day.
gideon_coal.wait: Coal. Fifteen. The hammer's still complaining.
done: Right. ...Hear that? That's the forge waking up.
Take this. Go on.

offer: A ruby.
...Don't ask what for. It's not for a gate.
gideon_ruby.yes: ...Thank you. Deep in the mine. Red, you'll know it.
gideon_ruby.wait: The ruby. If you find one.
done: ...That's the one. That's it exactly.
Here. A ring. Copper. I made two. Don't say anything.

offer: People say there's metal up there. On the moon. I think they're lying.
Prove me wrong. Bring me a shard.
gideon_moon.wait: Moon shard. If there's such a thing.
done: ...It's cold. It's cold to the touch and it rings when I... listen.
I was wrong. Here. That's for being wrong.

offer: Eight mushrooms for a tonic. The ordinary kind, the brown ones. Nothing fancy; I'm trying to help Bram sleep.
wren_mushrooms.yes: Thank you. The forest floor, or the meadow after rain.
wren_mushrooms.no: I'll tell Bram to count sheep. He'll count his customers instead.
wren_mushrooms.wait: Eight mushrooms. Brown ones. Bram's still not sleeping.
done: These are perfect. Firm caps.
Two potions for you. And Bram sends his thanks, in advance, from his future nap.

offer: There's a mushroom that glows. I know, Theo won't shut up about it either.
I don't want to write about it. I want to brew it. One cap, from the forest. You need a forager's eye to spot one.
wren_glowcap.yes: Look low, under the ferns. They hide from people who hurry.
done: It's warm. Feel it, it's warm.
I can do something with this. Here, for you, and a little of what I learned.

offer: Slime goo. Six. The grumps leave it everywhere and I think there's something in it.
Gloves. Please use gloves.
wren_slime.yes: Thank you. Jar it quick, it crawls.
wren_slime.no: I'll ask Rook. He'll bring it in a hat.
wren_slime.wait: Six goo. In a jar. Not a hat.
done: Still moving. Good. Good!
Energy tea, three. That's what the goo does, apparently. Don't tell anyone.

offer: Where the crystal came down, something grows. A flower with light in it.
One. Just one. I want to know what it does before Alder puts a fence round it.
wren_starflower.yes: Thank you. Be gentle with it. It's gentle with you.
done: Oh. Oh, it hums.
Here. And... I think I understand something now. Let me show you.

offer: The south bridge. Thirty stone. The boards are fine, it's the footings.
Finn fishes off it. Juniper crosses it. I'd like them both to keep doing that.
alder_bridge.yes: Thank you. The town pays. The town always pays, eventually.
alder_bridge.no: Understood. I'll put up a sign. People love a sign.
alder_bridge.wait: Thirty stone for the south bridge. The sign is up.
done: Footings done. Finn's already back on it. He didn't wait for the mortar.
Here. The town's thanks, and mine.

offer: The hall roof leaks on the council table. Right on my chair, in fact.
Forty wood. I'd ask Rook, but Rook and I have a history about a roof.
alder_wood.yes: Wonderful. Dry wood, please. The roof's had enough wet.
alder_wood.no: I'll move the chair. It's a start.
alder_wood.wait: Forty wood for the roof. The chair's still wet.
done: Dry. The chair is dry. I sat in it for an hour just to be sure.
Here. From a grateful, dry mayor.

offer: The fall fair. Five pumpkins, five cranberries, for the hall display. People come from the next valley for it.
Last year's pumpkins were... modest. I'd like immodest.
alder_fall_fair.no: We'll have a modest fair. Again.
alder_fall_fair.wait: Five and five for the fair. Immodest, remember.
done: Look at the size of that. People will talk. People will TALK.
Here. The fair's budget, most of it. You are the fair this year.

offer: A bottle of wine. A gift for the capital's inspector at the fair; they like a bottle to carry home.
...Discreetly. Bram talks.
alder_wine.no: Quite right. The inspector can make do with a handshake.
alder_wine.wait: The wine. For the inspector's gift.
done: Excellent. The inspector will carry it home and think well of us.
Here. With the council's thanks.

offer: The town bell's clapper split the night the red sky went over. It hasn't rung in twenty-one years.
A gold bar, and it rings again. For weddings. For warnings. For the end of the thing in the east.
alder_gold.yes: Then we'll hear it. All of us.
alder_gold.wait: The clapper. A gold bar, when you can bear to part with one.
done: ...Listen.
That's the bell. Thank you.

offer: Minnows. Five. I'm out of bait and too proud to buy it from myself.
finn_minnows.yes: Shallows, by the reeds. Little fella won't fight you.
finn_minnows.no: Fine. I'll use bread. Fish laugh at bread.
finn_minnows.wait: Five minnows. The fish are still laughing.
done: Good bait. Lively.
Here, ten of the good stuff. You're a fisherman now, whether you like it or not.

offer: Three trout. Another bet. Bram again. He's got a short memory.
Pie's bigger this time.
finn_trout.yes: That's the spirit. Deep water, early morning.
finn_trout.no: Bram wins twice in a row. I'll never hear the end.
done: THREE AGAIN. Bram's going to stop betting me and I'll have to find a hobby.
Your share. And you've got the touch now, I can see it.

offer: Four crabs. Bram's stew. He's got the pot on and no crab in it.
Beach, under the rocks. Mind the claws.
finn_crab.yes: Good. Quick, before the stew turns into soup.
finn_crab.wait: Four crabs for the stew. Mind the claws.
done: Still snapping. Good.
Bram says thanks. Here's what he paid me, which is now what I'm paying you.

offer: There's a pearl in the lake. Marlowe swears he's seen it from the top. Tomas always said there wasn't one.
I've fished that lake for thirty years. Maybe it wants somebody new.
finn_pearl.no: Maybe it's just a story. Most are.
finn_pearl.wait: The pearl. The lake's still keeping it.
done: ...It's real. Tomas, you were wrong. Same light Marlowe said.
I don't have words. I have crystals. Take them.

offer: Ten potatoes for seed stock. Mine went soft. Everything went soft this year except the goat.
hazel_potatoes.yes: Good. Firm ones. Eyes, not sprouts.
hazel_potatoes.no: I'll beg Maple. She'll make a face.
hazel_potatoes.wait: Ten potatoes, firm. Maple's already making the face.
done: Firm. Good eyes. These'll do a whole row.
Carrot seed, for you. Fair trade.

offer: Fifteen hay before the cold. Scythe the tall grass, it's everywhere, it's practically begging.
The goat eats hay. The goat eats everything.
hazel_hay.no: The goat will eat the fence again, then.
hazel_hay.wait: Fifteen hay. Winter's coming whether the goat likes it or not.
done: That's a winter. That's a whole winter right there.
Here. Hay money. Spend it on something that isn't hay.

offer: Six eggs. Mine are laying like they're on strike.
You'll want a coop for that. A coop's the best thing a person can build, after a fence.
hazel_eggs.yes: Good. Brown or white, I don't care, the goat doesn't care.
hazel_eggs.no: I'll ask Posy. She'll say she's out. She's always out.
hazel_eggs.wait: Six eggs. Build the coop if you haven't. Trust me.
done: Six. Warm. You've got good hens.
Corn seed for you. Hens like corn. So does the goat. Everyone likes corn.

offer: Four milk for the cheese cellar. I've got a wheel going and it's hungry.
You'll need a barn and a cow that likes you.
hazel_milk.no: The wheel will be a small wheel.
hazel_milk.wait: Four milk. The wheel's waiting. Cheese is patient. I'm not.
done: Rich. That's a happy cow.
Two wedges, aged. Don't eat them both at once. Or do.

offer: Six flour from the lake mill. Orla grinds it finer than anyone.
I'd go myself but the oven can't be left. It gets ideas.
posy_flour.yes: Thank you! Tell Orla it's for the braids.
posy_flour.no: I'll make do. Coarse bread. Honest bread.
posy_flour.wait: Six flour, from Orla. The oven's getting ideas.
done: Oh, feel that. Like silk.
Four loaves, still warm. Mind your fingers.

offer: Three honey for the spiced loaf. It's a once-a-year loaf. People plan around it.
posy_honey.yes: Wonderful. Dark honey if the bees have it.
posy_honey.no: The loaf will be... unspiced. Just loaf.
posy_honey.wait: Three honey. The spice is measured and waiting.
done: Smell that? That's the whole street turning its head.
The first slice is always for the person who brought the honey. Here.

offer: Twelve strawberries for jam. I know it's a lot. Jam is greedy.
posy_strawberries.yes: Thank you! Ripe, please. Jam knows.
posy_strawberries.no: I'll make less jam. The jars will be lonely.
posy_strawberries.wait: Twelve strawberries. The jars are lined up like soldiers.
done: Look at the colour! That's a summer in a jar.
Here. Jam money. And a jar from the last batch, for your trouble.

offer: Eight eggs. I'm out. I'm ALWAYS out, Hazel says, and she's right, and it's rude.
posy_eggs.yes: Thank you. Fresh. You can tell by the shine.
posy_eggs.no: Flat cakes, then. Sad, flat cakes.
posy_eggs.wait: Eight eggs. The cakes are waiting to rise.
done: Shiny! Fresh! Hazel can keep her remarks.
Here, and a cake, because the cakes rose.

offer: Ten mushrooms for the pot. Brown ones. Not the glowing ones, I don't want the stew glowing.
bram_mushrooms.yes: Good. Forest floor. Watch for the ones with spots, they're spiteful.
bram_mushrooms.wait: Ten mushrooms. Brown. The pot's on.
done: Good caps. Into the pot.
Here. And a bowl on the house, later.

offer: Five trail rations. Rook sells them, if he's in a selling mood. He usually isn't.
Or forage the hills and pack your own. I don't judge how the rations arrive.
bram_meat.wait: Five trail rations. Rook or the hills.
done: Now THAT'S a stew.
Here. For the rations. Worth it.

offer: Two bottles of wine for festival night. Gifts: one for the band, one for whoever sweeps the square after.
Wine's a thing you give, here. Nobody opens it till the harvest's in.
bram_wine.yes: Good. Grapes in a keg. Maple keeps grape seed back for friends, come fall.
bram_wine.no: The band gets a handshake again, then.
done: Good year. Good year! The band will frame theirs.
Here. And a slice of festival pie for you on the night.

offer: Ten wild herbs for the clinic. Cuts, scrapes, the usual. Children fall off everything.
juniper_herbs.yes: Thank you. The long grass, by the water.
juniper_herbs.no: I'll ration. Children will have to fall off less.
juniper_herbs.wait: Ten herbs. The cabinet's getting low.
done: Fresh. Thank you.
Two remedies for you. The children are grateful, in theory.

offer: Two glow-caps. I'm testing them on fever. The old books hint at it.
Wren and Theo will fight you for them. Bring them to me first.
juniper_glowcap.yes: Thank you. Forest, after dark. Be careful, truly.
juniper_glowcap.no: Sensible. The fever can wait, I suppose.
done: Both intact. Thank you, this could matter.
Here. If this works, you'll have helped more than me.

offer: Three bundles of shed fur.
Set a bramble brush on a trail, or pick the burrs yourself. Bring it clean.
done: ...Clean. Good.
Brushes. Two. You know how to set them now.

offer: Ten bones from the mine. The deep ones.
Arrowheads. Bone flies true.
rook_bones.no: Then I'll use stone. Stone's heavy.
done: Good bone.
Twenty arrows. Don't waste them.

offer: Grumps across the river. Orchard side. They're pulling the apples down.
Clear them. All of them. I'll know.
done: ...Quiet over there now.
Here. You track like one of us now. Don't let it go to your head.

offer: There's a book in the mine. An old one. A miner wrote it a hundred years ago and nobody's read it since.
Bring it up. I'll read it to you. Slowly, I'm afraid. The hand is terrible.
theo_book.yes: Wonderful. Every fifth floor or so, one of the old miners left a supply crate behind. Look in those.
theo_book.no: It's kept this long. It'll keep.
theo_book.wait: The book. In the mine. Still waiting to be read.
done: Oh... oh, look at this. He drew the tunnels. He drew where the crystal is. Was. Is.
Here. And... I think you should know what he knew. Let me teach you a little.

offer: Old coins. Three. The ones with the tower on them, from before the river moved.
Children find them. Children spend them on candy. It's a tragedy.
theo_coins.yes: Thank you. The mine, the ruins, the beach after a storm.
theo_coins.wait: Three old coins. Tower side up.
done: The tower, the tower, and... the tower with the bell. That's a rare one.
Here. The library's grateful. I'm grateful. The children are out three coins.

offer: A fossil. For the library case. The case has been empty for eleven years and it's become a sort of joke.
I'd like to stop being a joke.
theo_fossil.yes: Marvellous. Quarry, or the deep mine. Look for the swirls.
theo_fossil.wait: A fossil. The case is still empty.
done: ...Into the case. Lock it. There. Eleven years.
Here. You have no idea what you've done for me.

offer: Four sunflowers. Summer light, in a vase, on a windowsill. That's the painting.
I can see it. I just can't see it without them.
lumi_sunflowers.yes: Thank you. Big faces. Turned to the sun.
lumi_sunflowers.no: I'll paint the vase. Empty. Theo will say it's a statement.
lumi_sunflowers.wait: Four sunflowers. The vase is waiting on the sill.
done: Yes. YES. That's the light.
Here. Go and see it when it's dry, it's got you in it somewhere.

offer: A starflower. From the crater. I want to paint something that's actually alight.
Just one. I'll give it back to the ground after.
lumi_starflower.yes: Thank you. Hold it like a candle.
lumi_starflower.no: Alright. Some things shouldn't be painted.
lumi_starflower.wait: The starflower. For the one painting I'm afraid of.
done: ...It's lighting the canvas. It's lighting the whole room.
Here. I'll never sell that one. Come and see it.

offer: Three coffees. I'd sell my bench for them. Figure of speech. Mostly.
sal_coffee.wait: Coffee. Three. I'm running on fumes.
done: ...Oh. Oh, that's the stuff.
Here. It's not much. It's what I've got.

offer: Haven't eaten. Four bread would fix that.
Don't make it a thing.
done: ...That's good bread. Posy's?
I don't forget things like this. Remember that.

offer: Five fish. Minnows'll do. No questions.
done: ...There's a cat by the warehouse. Three legs. Don't tell anyone I feed it.
Here.

offer: I know a SECRET. A real one. Three candy and it's yours.
pip_candy.no: Your loss. It's a REALLY good secret.
done: Okay. Okay okay. The clock tower. There's a loose stone. There's a coin in it. THERE. I said it.
Here's the coin. Don't tell Theo I had it.

offer: Five shells from the beach. Big ones. I'm making a thing.
tobin_shells.no: Fine, I'll go myself. Dad says I can't. He's not here right now.
done: These are PERFECT. The thing is going to be amazing.
Here's my allowance. Don't tell Dad.

offer: Four flowers for a crown. I'm going to be queen of the fountain.
mabel_flowers.yes: Yay! Pink ones if you can!
mabel_flowers.no: Then I'll be queen of nothing. That's fine. That's FINE.
mabel_flowers.wait: Four flowers for the crown! The fountain is waiting for its queen!
done: It's PERFECT. Bow. You have to bow.
Here's... um... here's forty crystals. From the royal treasury. It's a jar.

offer: I need a frog. A LIVE one. Mum says no. So maybe just bait. Two bait, from Finn's shop. For the frog I don't have.
done: Wiggly! The frog I don't have is going to love them.
Here. I found these. Don't ask where.

offer: The lamp's been dark twenty winters. Ships still come. They just have to feel their way in.
Ten coal and I can fire the burner. It's a start. It's not the lens, but it's a start.
lighthouse_oil.yes: Thank you. The mountain, or the quarry. Hard black coal, not the soft stuff.
lighthouse_oil.wait: Ten coal, for the burner. The ships keep coming.
done: ...Hear that? The burner. She's breathing.
Here. It's not a lit lamp. But it's a warm one.

offer: The burner's warm but the lens is cracked. Light goes out of it like water through a basket.
A refined crystal, cut right, would throw that light to the horizon. Gideon can cut it. I can't afford it.
lighthouse_lens.yes: Then there'll be a light. Thank you.
lighthouse_lens.no: I understand. It's a lot to ask of a stranger.
lighthouse_lens.wait: The lens. A refined crystal. The horizon's still dark.
done: ...Look. LOOK at that. Over the water. Every ship for twenty miles can see us.
I don't know how to thank you. So I'll just keep it lit.

offer: Two salmon. I haven't had one since I took the post. They don't come up this far.
If you know a river that has them...
marlowe_salmon.yes: Thank you. Truly. The riverlands, maybe. Old Moss would know.
marlowe_salmon.no: That's alright. A man can live on crab.
marlowe_salmon.wait: Salmon. Two. The pan's been oiled for a year.
done: Oh. Oh, that's a fish.
Here. And come back at dusk, there'll be a second one on the fire and I don't eat alone well.

offer: That pup of yours follows you into the stalls. Clover doesn't mind. I mind.
Teach it to stay. Open the menu, Pup, tell it STAY. Then come back and I'll give you something for its trouble.
benno_pup_stay.yes: Good. A dog that stays is a dog that stays out of trouble.
benno_pup_stay.no: Then keep it out of my stalls.
benno_pup_stay.wait: Has it learned to stay yet? Menu, Pup, STAY. It's not hard. Clover learned it.
done: Sat right there, didn't it. Good dog. Good owner.
Treats. For the dog, not you.

offer: A dog can carry. Mine carried my lunch for six years and only ate it twice.
Tanning rack. Two shed fur, a rope, some wood. Make a pack and it'll haul for you.
benno_pup_pack.yes: Good. Rook sells the rack. Hill wolves leave shed fur on the brambles when you drive them off.
benno_pup_pack.no: Then you carry your own lunch.
benno_pup_pack.wait: The pack. Tanning rack. Shed fur, rope, wood.
done: Look at that. Proud as anything.
Here. And a bit of a tip for a job well made.

offer: Your dog's got teeth. Does it know what they're for?
Fight with it. Level three. Then we'll talk about collars.
done: ...Now that's a tracking dog.
Collar. Leather. I cut it myself.

offer: A dog that fights is useful. A dog that guards is worth its weight.
Level six. Then it can hold a door while you sleep.
rook_pup_guard.wait: Six. Guard Dog. Not there yet.
done: ...Mine was like that. Still is, on a good day.
Studded collar. Iron. Don't let it rust.

offer: The lamb's coming any day. The pen wants fresh bedding: ten bundles of fiber. Weeds give it, if you pull them.
tam_lamb.yes: Good. She'll thank you. Sheep thank you by not eating your hat.
tam_lamb.no: Then I'll pull weeds myself. Slowly.
done: That'll do her. Soft as anything.
Come by when she's born. You can name her. Not Dolly.

offer: Ten acorns. From the forest oaks. The marsh edge needs trees, and trees keep the fog honest.
moss_glowcaps.yes: Fat ones. The squirrels take the thin ones, and they're welcome to them.
moss_glowcaps.no: The fog will wait. So will I.
moss_glowcaps.wait: Ten acorns. Fat ones. Forest oaks.
done: Lovely. In they go, one by one, along the edge. Here: lamp oil. Light it where the fog's thickest and watch it back off.
I made that for myself, once.

offer: Ten bones from the deep floors, where the keeper sleeps. I want them out of my quarry's reputation.
granite_bones.yes: Bring them in a sack. Not your pockets.
done: Good riddance. Rook can have them for arrowheads; I'll have my reputation back.

offer: Three old coins, the ones from before the bell. They'd settle a question of dates.
done: These settle it. The bell is older than the town hall says.
Don't tell Alder. Or do. I'd like to see his face.

offer: There's a stone in the quarry, or down in the old mine, with a record in it. Same hand as the ruin walls. I need it to finish the sentence.
sel_fossil.yes: It looks like a fossil. It isn't.
sel_fossil.no: The sentence can stay unfinished a little longer.
sel_fossil.wait: The stone with the record in it.
done: ...it is about your field. The sentence. I was right.
I'll read you the rest when I've worked out the grammar.

offer: Marlowe won't walk round to the mill for bread, and he won't ask. Five wheat and I'll mill it and leave a loaf on his step.
orla_oil.yes: He'll pretend he didn't need it. Let him.
orla_oil.no: Then he'll eat ship's biscuit again. Stubborn man.
done: There. He'll have bread tonight and never know who to thank.
Take this. Don't argue with my knees.

offer: Summer pies. Everybody asks. Nobody grows blueberries. Six, and I'll put your name on the chalkboard.
posy_blueberries.yes: Tam has the canes, if you ask nicely. Or rudely; he doesn't notice.
posy_blueberries.no: Then it's rhubarb again. Nobody likes rhubarb.
done: Oh, they're perfect. Look at that blue.
Here: the first tart out of the oven. Don't tell the mayor.

offer: The library opens at eight. I open at nine, functionally. Old Moss says coffee grows here, if someone patient tried. Four beans?
theo_coffee.yes: Patience. A shrub, then a bean. Like research.
theo_coffee.no: Then I'll keep reading the same page.
theo_coffee.wait: Four coffee beans. Any kind. I'm not proud.
done: Coffee. Real coffee, here in this town.
Take this. It's a first edition. I have two.

offer: My pear trees died the year of the frost. Plant one; they rest in winter but they don't die. Bring me five pears and I'll believe in orchards again.
tam_orchard.yes: Trees are slow. That's the point of trees.
tam_orchard.no: Fair. It's a long promise, a tree.
done: These are good pears. Better than mine were.
Here: apple saplings. Start the orchard properly.

offer: There's a fever remedy that wants saffron. A thread of it. Old Moss sells the corms in autumn. Grow me one?
wren_saffron.yes: Autumn. Keep it watered. It sulks.
wren_saffron.no: Then I'll do without, and so will someone.
done: That's it. That's the colour.
Two remedies, for your pack. You'll need them more than you think.

offer: The footbridge is two bad boards from being a ford. Twenty planks. A sawhorse on your farm will do it: two logs a plank.
hazel_planks.yes: The Plans board by your house has the sawhorse. Build it or I'll sell you one.
hazel_planks.no: Then mind your step on the bridge.
done: Straight and dry. You've a carpenter's eye.
Nails, for your own building. You'll want them: everything bigger than a bench eats nails.

offer: The clock tower's stuck at ten past. Four gears. Not mine: yours. I want to see what your anvil can do.
gideon_gears.yes: One iron bar a gear, on your own anvil. Your mining has to be up to it.
gideon_gears.wait: Four gears, off your own anvil.
done: Teeth are even. Huh.
Horseshoes. Nail one over your door. The other's for when the first falls on your head.

offer: I've run out of canvas and I refuse to paint on a door again. Six linen. Flax and a loom; it's practically meditation.
lumi_linen.yes: Spring flax. Two stalks a bolt.
done: Oh, the weave on these.
Paint. Colour something on your farm. It's very brown out there.

offer: Strangers across the river. Orchard side. Coats too good for picking apples.
Run them off. Every one. I'll know.
rook_tracks@gangsters.wait: The orchard. Those coats. Still there.

offer: Slime goo. Six. The slimes leave it everywhere and I think there's something in it.
Gloves. Please use gloves.
Moonwort. One sprig, from Orchard Hills, north of the forest. The blue one.
If you're going out that way. If.
wren_moonwort.no: It'll keep. It's kept this long.
wren_moonwort.wait: The blue herb. Orchard Hills. Moonwort.
done: That's it. That's the blue.
I'll make the fever draught before I lose my nerve.

offer: Moonwort. The blue that grows up in Orchard Hills, past the forest. I've tried to mix it for a year.
Bring me a sprig and I'll stop trying.
lumi_moonwort.yes: You're a saint. A muddy one, soon.
lumi_moonwort.no: The blue can wait. I'm used to it.
lumi_moonwort.wait: Still no blue. The canvas is judging me.
done: Oh. Oh, that's the colour.
Don't watch me cry into the turpentine.

offer: Two root beers for festival night. One for me, one for Posy's mother. She always had the first of the summer.
The soda fountain on the avenue makes them. I never get there.
bram_rootbeer.yes: Good. Cold, if you can manage it.
bram_rootbeer.no: Another year, then. Every year I mean to.
bram_rootbeer.wait: Two root beers. The festival's coming.
done: Good fizz. She'd have liked that.
Here. And a slice of festival pie for you on the night.

offer: You've been to the Rec Center? Bet you can't bowl a hundred and twenty.
I'll give you my whole allowance if you do. Okay, Dad's whole allowance. Okay, Dad will pay.
rec_bowl_120.yes: Ha! Lane two's luckiest. Everybody knows that.
rec_bowl_120.wait: A hundred and twenty! Not a hundred and nineteen. I'll know.
done: You did NOT. ...You did? The board says you did.
Fine. Dad, pay up. A deal's a deal.

offer: The Teddy Bear. At the prize counter. With the bow.
I need eighty tickets and I have four. Could you win it for me? Please? I'll give you my kite. I'll win another kite.
rec_teddy.yes: THANK YOU. Name him something good.
rec_teddy.no: ...He'll still be there. Probably. Unless Pip gets him.
rec_teddy.wait: Is he still there? The bear? With the bow?
done: You got him! He's softer than I thought! He's PERFECT.
Here, the kite's yours. I mean it. Bears are better than kites.

offer: You been up the Rec Hall? Bet you can't bowl a hundred and twenty.
Do it and Dad pays you. He says everybody in this town owes somebody. Now he owes you.
done: You did NOT. ...The chalk wall says you did.
Fine. Dad, pay up. A deal's a deal.

offer: The Teddy Bear. At the Rec Hall counter. With the bow.
I need eighty tickets and I have four. Win him for me? I'll give you my kite.
Block Jumper level three has a gap that is IMPOSSIBLE. Like, actually impossible.
If you clear it I'll give you my tickets. Some of my tickets. Forty tickets!
rec_pip_jumper.yes: Jump at the LAST second. Or the first. I don't know, that's why I'm asking.
rec_pip_jumper.no: Okay. I'll keep falling in the gap. It's fine.
rec_pip_jumper.wait: Level three yet? The gap? THE GAP?
done: You cleared it? Show me how! ...Okay, don't, I'll work it out.
Here, forty tickets. A deal's a deal.

offer: I've written down a pattern for Crystal Stack. Flat rows first, a well on the right, wait for the long gem.
I can't test it. My hands panic. Would you score three thousand with it, for science?
rec_theo_stack.yes: Flat rows. Right-hand well. Patience. Report back.
rec_theo_stack.no: The pattern will wait. Patterns are patient.
rec_theo_stack.wait: Three thousand points on Crystal Stack. The pattern holds, I'm nearly sure.
done: Three thousand! The pattern holds. I'm writing a footnote with your name in it.
Take this for your trouble. Science pays. A little.

offer: Our class has a chart of Duck Pond scores and mine is the lowest. By a LOT.
If you get three hundred I can say a friend did it. That counts. I asked.
rec_wren_jr_duck.yes: Pop the gold ducks, they're worth more! Mum says aim small.
rec_wren_jr_duck.no: Okay. The chart can stay sad.
rec_wren_jr_duck.wait: Three hundred on Duck Pond! For the chart!
done: Three hundred! I'm putting a star next to it. A big one.
These are my saved tickets. You earned them.

offer: There's a board over Whack-a-Grump. Top score's four hundred and the initials are rude.
Knock them off. I'll make it worth your while.
rec_sal_whack.yes: Bop the grumps, leave the bunnies. The bunnies cost you.
rec_sal_whack.no: Rude initials stay up, then. Your call.
rec_sal_whack.wait: Four hundred on Whack-a-Grump. The board's still rude.
done: Four hundred. The board's clean. Good work.
Tickets, and something for luck. You'll need it on the lanes.

offer: You beat Tobin's bet, I hear. That's sweet, dear. Tobin is eleven.
League night is the third day of every week. Bowl a hundred and fifty and I'll treat you like a real rival.
rec_maple_league.yes: Lane one is mine. You can have lane two.
rec_maple_league.no: Scared of an old lady with a heavy ball. Sensible.
rec_maple_league.wait: A hundred and fifty, dear. League night's the third day of the week.
done: A hundred and fifty! Well. Gideon owes me a pie, he bet against you.
Here, from the league kitty. Don't tell the league.

offer: The arcade cabinets are the town's pride and I have personally tried... one.
Would you play every cabinet once and tell me they all work? The town will reward diligence!
rec_alder_cabinets.no: Another day, then. They're not going anywhere. They're bolted down.
rec_alder_cabinets.wait: Every cabinet, once! For the public good.
done: Every cabinet works! Diligence! Civic spirit!
A small reward from the town purse, and tickets from the front desk.

offer: The Rec Hall cabinets keep this town calm, and I have personally tried... one.
Play every cabinet once and tell me they all work. The town pays for diligence, whatever else it's paying for.
done: Every cabinet works. Good. A town that plays doesn't fight.
Something from the town purse, and tickets from the front desk.

offer: Board over Whack-a-Snitch. Top score's four hundred and the initials are from a crew I don't like.
Knock them off. I'll make it worth your while.
rec_sal_whack@gangsters.yes: Bop the snitches, leave the bunnies. The bunnies cost you.
rec_sal_whack@gangsters.wait: Four hundred on Whack-a-Snitch. Their initials are still up.
done: Four hundred. Their initials are gone. They'll notice. Good.
Tickets, and something for luck.

offer: Our class has a chart of Neon Range scores and mine is the lowest. By a LOT.
If you get three hundred I can say a friend did it. That counts. I asked.
rec_wren_jr_duck@gangsters.yes: Hit the gold targets, they're worth more! Mum says aim small.
rec_wren_jr_duck@gangsters.wait: Three hundred on Neon Range! For the chart!
done: Three hundred! I'm putting a star next to it. A big one.
These are my saved tickets. You earned them.

offer: I've written down a pattern for Neon Stack. Flat rows first, a well on the right, wait for the long bar.
I can't test it. My hands panic. Would you score three thousand with it, for science?
rec_theo_stack@gangsters.wait: Three thousand points on Neon Stack. The pattern holds, I'm nearly sure.

offer: The bell is gone; only the hook is left. But a bell is just copper that has learned to sing.
Three bars of copper. Smelt them in your furnace and bring them to me; the old monastery can have its voice back.
catkins_bell.yes: Three bars. Mind they're copper, not tin. Tin sulks.
catkins_bell.no: The courtyard has been quiet for an age. It can wait a little longer.
catkins_bell.wait: Three Copper Bars, for the monastery bell.
done: Copper. Warm already. I'll take it up the stair tonight.
When you hear a bell at dusk, that's the courtyard saying thank you. And me. Mostly me.

offer: Theo has a museum now! A real one, with glass cases!
Could you put a fossil in it? I want to see one with a little card under it.
coll_pip_fossil.no: Okay. But the cases look so empty...
coll_pip_fossil.wait: A fossil, in the museum tray! Theo does the card.
done: I saw it! It has a card and everything!
I read the card four times. Here, I saved this for you.

offer: Theo's got tanks in that museum, and nothing swimming in them.
Five kinds of fish in there and I'll stock you up on bait.
coll_finn_tanks.wait: Five kinds in the tanks. Any five.
done: Saw the tanks. Looks like a proper aquarium now.
Bait, as promised.

offer: Theo turned the east wing into a Curio Room! With glass cases!
Could you put a fossil in there? I want to see it with a little card.
Theo's got tanks in that Curio Room and nothing swimming in them.
Five kinds of fish in there and I'll stock you up on bait.
Beat Tobin's bet, I hear. Tobin is eleven.
League night's the third day of every week, upstairs at the Rec Hall. Bowl a hundred and fifty and I'll treat you like a real rival.
rec_maple_league@gangsters.yes: Lane one is mine. You can have lane two.
rec_maple_league@gangsters.no: Scared of an old woman with a heavy ball. Smart.
rec_maple_league@gangsters.wait: A hundred and fifty. League night's the third day of the week.
done: A hundred and fifty. Gideon owes me a pie; he bet against you.
From the league kitty. The league doesn't need to know.

offer: Wood first, I said. I meant it.
Eight pieces of Hardwood. I'm building a window seat. Don't ask who for.
tess_seat.yes: Good. Straight grain if you can find it. I'll know if you can't.
done: ...That's good timber.
Measure twice. I'll take it from here.

offer: The moth nets are fraying and the moths keep wandering off to the Glade.
Five Wisp Thread would mend them. The glade wisps leave it everywhere.
mega_gloamwood_job.yes: You're a dear. Mind the slimes, they're sticky.
done: Perfect. Bartholomew says thank you. Bartholomew is the moth.

offer: The Sunken Temple's full of carved scarabs. Gold ones. They're the key to the whole script.
Two would do. I'd go myself but I'm a scholar, not a hero.
mega_sunscorch_job.yes: Wonderful! Mind the glass golems. They don't mind you.
done: Look at the wings! It's a calendar. The whole beetle is a calendar.

offer: Sunstones hold the day's heat all night. Four of them under the lamp-posts and the well stays lit till dawn.
The Dune Sea and the Glass Canyon have them, if you can crack the rocks.
mega_sunscorch_rahim.yes: Good. Mind the hounds. They like shiny things too.
done: Feel that? Warm as noon. The caravans will see the Post from three dunes off now.

offer: The Baron's bots wrecked the yard switch. No switch, no trains, no Junction.
Four Rail Chain and two cans of Engine Oil. The bots carry both.
mega_ironline_job.yes: Good. Hit 'em where the rivets are.
done: She switches! Hear that clunk? That's freedom, that is.

offer: I want a window that never frosts over. Rime Crystal for the frame, Glacier Glass for the pane.
Three crystals and two glass. The Caverns and the Glacier have both.
mega_frostpeak_job.yes: Wrap up warm. The golems don't feel the cold, but you do.
done: Look at that view. I can see the Summit from my stove! Here, something for your trouble.

offer: The winds are getting wilder every day. I can calm them, with the right weather in a jar.
Three Storm Glass and two Storm Fluff. The Storm Shelf has plenty.
mega_windward_job.yes: Splendid. Don't hold anything metal up there.
done: Feel that? A breeze. Just a breeze. Take this, you'll need it on the Shelf.

offer: I'm painting Gilt City as it really is. For that I need real gold leaf and a real pearl.
Three Gold Leaf and one Pearl Necklace. The Vaults have both, if you're brave.
mega_giltcity_job.yes: Wonderful. Wear something dark, the guards hate that.
done: Perfect. Look at it shine! She'll hate it. Here, for you.
